surprises.description: Pulmonx reported $22.8 million of revenue, about 4% above the $21.93 million consensus and 6% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s implied 2%. The return to growth was expected, but the growth rate and revenue beat were stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Worldwide revenue was $22.8 million, a 6% increase over the prior year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “consensus $21.93M implies the first year-over-year revenue growth (+2.0%)”

surprises.description: The quarterly adjusted EBITDA loss was substantially smaller than the preview’s estimated $5.5 million loss: Pulmonx reported a $3.5 million loss, nearly 60% narrower year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed nearly 60% year-over-year to $3.5 million.”

surprises.description: The net loss per share was $0.19, a smaller loss than the preview’s $0.26 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “net loss improved 40% to $8.4 million ($0.19 loss per share versus $0.34 prior year).”

surprises.description: U.S. revenue reached $14.9 million, above the preview’s $13.8–$14.3 million estimate range, and grew 7% year over year. The preview highlighted positive U.S. growth as a key question, but its base case expected U.S. revenue to be roughly flat year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. $13.8–14.3M”; “Base ... U.S. roughly flat YoY”; “U.S. revenue YoY turning positive.”

surprises.description: Pulmonx added only 8 U.S. treating centers, below the preview’s watchpoint of at least 12 for the quarter and its roughly 40-per-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “8 new U.S. treating centers added during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “treating center adds ≥12 (Q2 pace) against the ~40/year target”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year gross margin guidance to approximately 77%, above the prior approximately 76% guide the preview expected to remain in force.

Full-year operating expense guidance came down to $108–$109 million, below the preview’s expected $109–$111 million range; the stated stock-based compensation estimate also fell to about $14 million from about $15 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full year 2026 OpEx now expected between $108 million and $109 million including ~$14 million of stock-based compensation.”

surprises.description: Expected full-year cash burn improved modestly to roughly $22 million, compared with the preview’s expected $23 million cash decrease.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year 2026 cash burn is expected to be roughly $22 million, a 30% reduction from 2025.”
